A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the defect engineering strategy is a promising approach to design and develop new MOF based catalysts for the aerobic oxidation of alcohols.
the defect engineered MOF HKUST 1 can be used as an efficient support for the preparation of metal nanoparticles with controlled size and spatial distribution.
the incorporation of a defect generating linker in HKUST 1 leads to the formation of micro and mesoporous materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to control the spatial distribution of NPs by tuning the amount of the linker incorporated in the MOFs, thus allowing for the design of a new generation of catalysts with enhanced catalytic properties.
the defect engineering of MOFs is not only a means for the introduction of new functionality into the material but also for the control of the size and spatial arrangement of metal nanoparticles.
the defect engineering of MOFs can be used as a tool to control the size and spatial location of NPs in MOFs.
